curation.lead:
Josh Kushner is the founder and managing partner of Thrive Capital, a New York-based venture capital firm he established in 2009. He is also co-founder and vice chairman of Oscar Health (NYSE: OSCR), a technology-driven health insurance company that went public in March 2021. As of November 2024, SEC filings show Kushner beneficially owns approximately 17.2 percent of Oscar Health shares, held across nine Thrive Capital fund vehicles, with Class B super-voting shares giving him approximately 77 percent of the company's combined voting power [Finding #4342].

Thrive Capital has made multi-round investments in OpenAI totaling over $2 billion, from an initial 2023 position at a $27 billion valuation through a December 2025 investment at $285 billion [Finding #4367]. In December 2025 OpenAI in turn took an ownership stake in Thrive Holdings, a separate Kushner-controlled vehicle that acquires and operates companies [Finding #4368]. According to Oscar Health product announcements, the company has deployed OpenAI models in production for member healthcare support [Finding #4373]. Thrive Holdings also launched Shield Technology Partners in June 2025 with over $100 million in initial funding, hiring former Palantir CIO Jim Siders as CEO [Finding #4370].

Kushner's FEC donor history is exclusively Democratic, including $250,000 to Growth Democrats hybrid PAC in 2024, as well as earlier donations to Beto for Texas (2018) and the NJ Democratic State Committee (2014) [Finding #4327]. This diverges from the Republican giving of his father Charles Kushner and brother Jared Kushner, though the three share overlapping business interests through family real estate holdings [Finding #4327]. LittleSis records Joel Cutler of General Catalyst as a mentor to Josh Kushner; General Catalyst is also an Oscar Health investor [Finding #4374].
curation.system_role: Kushner occupies an interconnected position as controlling shareholder of a publicly traded health insurer, lead investor across multiple OpenAI funding rounds, and founder of a holding company in which OpenAI has taken an equity stake, creating a structure where his venture firm is simultaneously an investor in, a strategic partner of, and through Oscar Health an enterprise customer of the same AI company.

sections.title: Thrive Capital Structure and SEC Filings
sections.content:
Thrive Capital's fund architecture spans at least fifteen SEC-registered entities: Thrive Capital Partners II through VII LPs, corresponding GP LLCs for funds II through VI, and Claremount V, VI, and TW co-investment vehicles, all New York-based and Delaware-incorporated [Finding #4337]. Kushner is the sole managing member of each GP vehicle, replicating the single-controller structure used by his brother Jared Kushner across Affinity Partners [Finding #4337]. EDGAR records Kushner's personal CIK (0001844181) with Form 3 and Form 4 insider transaction filings for Oscar Health (OSCR) and Vimeo (VMEO) [Finding #4337]. Thrive filed an SC 13D for Oscar Health in August 2021 upon the company's March 2021 IPO and has filed amendments through November 2024, indicating continuous 5%-or-greater ownership through that date [Finding #4337]. The firm's registered address is 295 Lafayette Street, 7th Floor, New York, NY 10012 [Finding #4342].

According to fund reporting, Thrive closed its ninth flagship fund, Thrive IX, in 2024, raising $5 billion and targeting early-stage healthcare and AI startups [Finding #4373].

sections.title: Oscar Health: Ownership and Voting Control
sections.content:
Kushner co-founded Oscar Health and held the title Co-Founder and Vice Chairman as of November 2024 [Finding #4342]. His SC 13D/A Amendment 3 (filed November 13, 2024) discloses beneficial ownership of 42,875,786 shares, composed primarily of 32,859,064 Class B shares [Finding #4342]. Because Class B shares carry 20 votes each while Class A shares carry one vote each, Kushner's 17.2 percent economic interest translates to approximately 77 percent of combined voting power across Oscar Health's two-class capital structure [Finding #4342]. This dual-class structure is held across nine Thrive Capital fund vehicles, meaning voting control over a publicly traded company is consolidated in one person through a private fund structure rather than through personal direct holdings [Finding #4342].

Thrive VII Growth holds $35 million in Oscar Health's 7.25% convertible notes due 2031, adding a debt exposure on top of the equity position [Finding #4342]. In November 2024 Kushner made open-market Rule 10b-18 purchases totaling approximately $18.5 million, at prices between $13 and $17 per share [Finding #4342]. According to Oscar Health product announcements, the company has since deployed OpenAI models in its Oswell AI agent for member support, and Thrive Capital job listings show multiple AI product and engineering roles [Finding #4373].

sections.title: OpenAI Investment and Thrive-OpenAI Circular Structure
sections.content:
Thrive Capital made its first investment in OpenAI in 2023 at a $27 billion valuation [Finding #4367]. In October 2024 Thrive led OpenAI's $6.6 billion funding round at a $157 billion post-money valuation [Finding #4367]. In December 2025 Thrive invested approximately $1 billion in a further OpenAI round at a $285 billion valuation, described by CNBC as a preferential deal for a long-time backer [Finding #4367]. Total Thrive investment across the three rounds exceeds $2 billion by the public reporting dates [Finding #4367].

In December 2025 OpenAI announced it was taking an ownership stake in Thrive Holdings, Kushner's separate vehicle that buys and operates companies [Finding #4368]. As part of the arrangement OpenAI agreed to embed engineering, research, and product teams inside Thrive Holdings portfolio companies [Finding #4368]. Kushner described the goal as extending the OpenAI partnership to deploy frontier models in sectors with large addressable markets [Finding #4368]. Cross-reference of these filings and Oscar Health product records indicates that Thrive Capital is an equity holder in OpenAI while OpenAI is simultaneously an equity holder in a Thrive-controlled entity and a technology provider to Oscar Health, a company Kushner controls [Finding #4368] [Finding #4373].

The OpenAI relationship also connects indirectly to SoftBank Group, which invested $40 billion in OpenAI and co-founded the $500 billion Stargate infrastructure project with OpenAI and Oracle [Connection #2592]. Kushner's equity in OpenAI positions him within a shareholder group that includes SoftBank as the second-largest investor [Connection #2592].

sections.title: Thrive Holdings and Shield Technology Partners
sections.content: Thrive Holdings is a vehicle Kushner launched to acquire, own, and operate companies directly—distinct from Thrive Capital's fund model of minority equity stakes [Finding #4368]. In June 2025 Thrive Holdings co-founded Shield Technology Partners alongside ZBS Partners with over $100 million in initial funding [Finding #4370]. Shield acquires ownership stakes in IT services companies and integrates AI capabilities using the OpenAI partnership; its internal platforms, Sentinel and Spectre, automate IT ticket resolution [Finding #4370]. In December 2025 Shield hired Jim Siders as CEO; Siders spent twelve years as CIO at Palantir Technologies before joining Shield [Finding #4370]. As of December 2025 Shield operated across seven acquired companies generating over $100 million in combined revenue [Finding #4370]. In February 2026 Thrive Holdings made a further $100 million investment in Shield [Finding #4370].

sections.title: Political Activity and Family Network
sections.content:
Kushner's FEC contribution history runs exclusively to Democratic candidates and committees: $150,000 to Growth Democrats hybrid PAC on February 7, 2024, and $100,000 to Growth Democrats on April 22, 2024, both filed with occupation listed as Investor and Founder and Managing Partner at Thrive Capital [Finding #4327]. Earlier contributions include a donation to Beto for Texas in 2018 and to the NJ Democratic State Committee in 2014 [Finding #4327]. His father Charles Kushner has contributed approximately $420,000 to Republican causes and entities; his brother Jared Kushner has made contributions to Republican state parties [Finding #4327]. Despite the divergent political giving, FEC records and LittleSis data show the three share overlapping business interests through family real estate holdings [Finding #4327].

LittleSis entity 102209 maps Kushner's network to include Joel Cutler of General Catalyst as mentor—General Catalyst is also an Oscar Health investor through its IRA fund—as well as connections to Alan Dershowitz (student relationship), a co-founding role in Cadre (an online real estate investment platform built with Jared Kushner), investments in Forward Healthcare and Art.sy, and education at Harvard College and Harvard Business School [Finding #4374].

open_questions: What is the precise ownership percentage OpenAI holds in Thrive Holdings, and do any side letters or information rights under that arrangement give OpenAI visibility into Thrive Capital fund strategy or portfolio company data? [Finding #4368]

Does Oscar Health's commercial relationship with OpenAI—using OpenAI models in the Oswell member support agent—operate on arm's-length pricing, and what, if any, preferential terms were negotiated given Thrive Capital's position as a lead investor across OpenAI's funding rounds? [Finding #4373]

How are the nine Thrive Capital fund vehicles that collectively hold Oscar Health Class B shares structured across vintage funds, and which limited partners in those funds therefore hold indirect voting exposure to the insurer's operations? [Finding #4342]

What is the scope of the embedding arrangement under which OpenAI places engineering and product teams inside Thrive Holdings portfolio companies, and does Shield Technology Partners' defense-adjacent positioning (via Palantir CIO hire) affect the terms of that arrangement? [Finding #4368] [Finding #4370]

Kushner co-founded Cadre with Jared Kushner as a real estate investment platform; given Jared Kushner's post-White House fundraising activity and Cadre's subsequent restructuring, what is the current ownership and operational relationship between Josh Kushner, Thrive Capital, and Cadre? [Finding #4374]
